al-jaffee: # al-jaffee Fold-in compaction for pi, named after MAD magazine's Al Jaffee and his fold-ins: the page folds to a marker, only the summary shows, and you can fold it back out when you need the whole picture. The agent marks a point in the conversation (`set_fold_marker`), runs a self-contained tangent, then calls `fold(summary)`. At the end of that turn the session tree branches back to the marker and the summary is written as the marker call's new result — the tangent leaves the live context entirely, and the agent continues the main line as if the tangent had been one tool call. The folded transcript is not deleted — sessions are append-only trees, so the tangent stays on a branch. `return_to_fold(prompt, fold?)` navigates back to it with an agent-provided prompt; `/tree` shows the folds

airspeak: # airspeak This pi/oh-my-pi extension brings the mechanical writing discipline of ASD-STE100 to agent-written Markdown. It is a machine-checkable constraint set enforced inside the write loop. It comes in two parts: 1. **Lint extension** (omp): checks every `*.md` / `*.mdx` / `*.markdown` file you write or edit (plus extensionless README/CHANGELOG/RELEASE/errors/runbooks) and reports violations with rule references. 2. **Writing-style skill** (any Agent-Skills-capable agent): the full rule guidance, installable in Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, and Google Gemini CLI.
